info.title: Revcenter API
info.description: Search, enrich, and activate people and companies. Two authentication surfaces share one host: the bearer-token API under `/v1` for server-to-server and agent use, and the workspace-session API under `/api` that the Revcenter app itself runs on.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Web search, search runs, results, exports, and shareable shortlists.

tags.name: People
tags.description: Person search, profile enrichment, and the workspace contact pool.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: Company search, company enrichment, and org-chart people.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: Plan, publish, and launch outbound sequences on Smartlead and HeyReach.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Health, usage totals, and cost events.

post.description:
Runs a web search and returns organic results plus the raw provider response. Billed per request as a metered acquisition event.

Requires the `data:search:web` scope.

query.description: The search query. `q` is accepted as an alias.
examples: site:linkedin.com/in wealth advisor San Jose CFP

num.description: Results per page. Requests of 10 or fewer bill at the shallow rate; more than 10 bills at the deep rate.

location.description: Geographic location string passed through to the search provider.

idempotencyKey.description: Deduplicates billing when a request is retried. The `Idempotency-Key` header does the same thing.

linkedinSourcing.summary: Sourcing query scoped to LinkedIn profiles

value.query: site:linkedin.com/in wealth advisor San Jose CFP impact investing

results.description: Organic results, when the surface returns them.

response.description: The unmodified provider response, so surfaces without an `organic` array are still fully available.

post.description:
Searches LinkedIn people by keyword, company, location, or name. At least one criterion other than `page` is required.

Requires the `data:people:search` scope.

companyId.description: LinkedIn company identifier to scope the search to.

geoId.description: LinkedIn geo identifier. More precise than `location`.

200.description: Matching profiles, one page at a time.

get.description:
Returns a full LinkedIn profile.

The path segment is interpreted for you: a public identifier (`dahn-lincoln`), a numeric profile ID, or a URL-encoded LinkedIn URL all work. Query parameters override the path when you want to be explicit.

Requires the `data:people:read` scope.

parameters.name: profileId
parameters.description: Public identifier, numeric profile ID, or URL-encoded LinkedIn profile URL.

parameters.name: linkedin_url
parameters.description: Full LinkedIn profile URL. Takes precedence over the path segment. `url` is accepted as an alias.

parameters.name: public_identifier
parameters.description: LinkedIn public identifier, used when the path segment is a placeholder.

post.description:
Searches LinkedIn companies by keyword, location, or headcount band. At least one criterion other than `page` is required.

Requires the `data:companies:search` scope.

companySize.description: Headcount band as the provider expresses it.

200.description: Matching companies, one page at a time.

get.description:
Returns a full company record. The path segment is treated as the LinkedIn universal name unless you pass `search`.

Requires the `data:companies:read` scope.

parameters.name: universal_name
parameters.description: Explicit universal name. Overrides the path segment.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Resolve the company by name search instead of by universal name. Takes precedence when present.

get.description: Confirms the API is reachable and your key authenticates. Requires a valid key but no scope, and is never billed.

Lifetime totals for every API-key request in the workspace. App activity is excluded — only calls made with an API key are counted.

Requires the `usage:read` scope.

The individual metered events behind the totals, newest first. Match `request_id` against the `meta.request_id` of the call that produced it.

Requires the `usage:read` scope.

post.description: Turns a job description or plain-language brief into structured criteria, without running a search. Use the returned `criteria` as the body of `POST /api/scans` once a human has reviewed it.

examples: Clinic manager in Lévis, Québec. French required. 5+ years managing a multi-site clinic. Find 25.

entityCoverage.description: Which criteria dimensions the input actually pinned down — drives the confirmation chips in the app.

familyUnresolved.description: True when the role sits outside the known role-family taxonomy. The role name is preserved as a title variant.

post.description:
Creates a search and starts the pipeline. Returns immediately with a `scanId` — the run continues in the background, so poll `GET /api/scans/{id}` for status and results.

A target count written into `rawInput` ("find 25") is parsed out and used as the run's target.

rawInput.description: The original brief. Kept for provenance and parsed for a target count.

projectId.description: Attach the run to a client project so its context and disqualifiers apply.

201.description: The run was created and is executing.

get.description: The 100 most recent searches in the workspace, newest first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text filter. Matches both the generated title and the prompt the user actually wrote.

parameters.name: sector
parameters.description: Restrict to one sector. Unknown values are ignored.

get.description:
The full state of one search: the record itself, per-stage run history, and ranked candidates. Client-mode searches additionally return discovered companies and decision-maker leads.

Poll this while `scan.status` is `running`.

200.description: The search, its runs, and its results.

get.description: Just the prompt a search ran on — cheap enough to fetch when reopening a past search in intake to copy or rerun it.

200.description: The prompt and its identifying context.

post.description:
Reruns the pipeline on an existing candidate search to pull more results against the same criteria. Returns immediately; the run continues in the background.

Rejected with `409` if the search is already running, or if it is a client-mode search — those re-run through approval instead.

Runs the contact waterfall over a completed search to attach emails and phone numbers. This spends money, so it is deliberately gated: completed searches only, on an explicit call, with an explicit target.

Records a human accept / reject / maybe on one candidate. Send `null` to clear a verdict.

Every call also writes a candidate feedback event — the verdict, the reason codes, the rank the candidate was shown at, its score and subscores, and a snapshot of the criteria it was judged against. That trail is what scoring quality is measured and tuned against, so reason codes are worth sending.

parameters.name: candidateId
parameters.description: The candidate's ID, as returned in `candidates[].candidate.id`.

verdict.description: `null` clears the verdict and logs a `verdict_cleared` event.

reasonCodes.description: Why. `reason_codes` is accepted as an alias.

source.description: Where the verdict came from, for attribution in the feedback log.

post.description:
Snapshots a shortlist into a passwordless link anyone can open — no Revcenter account needed. The snapshot is frozen at creation: later changes to the search do not alter what a recipient sees, and contact details are stripped from the public payload.

Only completed candidate searches can be shared. Scores below 80 are never shareable, whatever selection mode you use.

selectionMode.description: `top_n` takes the highest-ranked `limit` leads, `all_qualified` takes every lead at or above `minScore`, and `manual` takes exactly the `candidateIds` you name.

limit.description: Used by `top_n` only. Clamped to 1–500, so lists well past 80 leads are fine.

minScore.description: Score floor. Values below 80 are raised to 80.

shared.description: How many leads the snapshot contains.

get.description:
Resolves a share token into its frozen shortlist. **No authentication** — the token is the credential, so treat share URLs as secrets.

The prompt behind the search is included so a recipient can see what was actually asked for. Each read increments the view counter. Responses are sent `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The share token from the link.

rawInput.description: The prompt the search ran on.

candidates.description: Public candidate records. Emails and phone numbers are always null here.

get.description: Downloads the search's results as a CSV file, including any contact details already enriched onto them.

post.description:
Extracts criteria from up to 10 job descriptions and runs each as its own search, two pipelines in flight at a time. Returns immediately with a `batchId`.

One bad job description fails its own search and never the batch.

items.description: Job descriptions. Entries shorter than 12 characters are dropped before the cap is applied.

label.description: Title for the resulting search. Falls back to the first 120 characters of `text`.

items.label: Clinic Manager — Lévis
items.text: Clinic manager in Lévis, Québec. French required. 5+ years running a multi-site clinic.

items.label: Wealth Advisor — San Jose
items.text: Wealth advisor, San Jose. CFP preferred, 7+ years, book of business.

queued.description: How many job descriptions were accepted.

get.description: The 20 most recent bulk batches in the workspace, newest first.
One batch and every search it spawned, in submission order. Poll this to watch a batch finish.

The workspace's deduplicated person pool — everyone who has ever appeared in a search, collapsed to one record each, with paging and facet filters.

Repeatable filter parameters are AND-ed across facets and OR-ed within one facet.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Anything other than these values falls back to 25.

parameters.name: contact
parameters.description: Repeatable. Filter by which contact details are present.

parameters.name: minScans
parameters.description: Only people who appeared in at least this many searches.

200.description: A page of contacts with facet counts.

get.description: Every firm that has surfaced in this workspace's searches, deduplicated, with the count of people attached to each. Capped at 500 firms.
The org chart Revcenter has assembled for one firm: everyone attached to it across this workspace's searches, deduplicated. Capped at 200 rows.

title.description: The title as it appears on the org chart.

post.description:
Step one of two. Turns a plain-language brief plus a set of searches into a reviewable campaign spec, and preflights the workspace against it.

Nothing is pushed to Smartlead or HeyReach here. The `issues` array is the point: it surfaces every setup problem — missing API key, no connected inbox or sender, no eligible leads — before anyone can publish.

prompt.description: What the campaign should do, in plain language.
examples: Four-touch LinkedIn sequence for the Lévis clinic managers, warm and short, two days apart.

scanIds.description: The searches to draw leads from. Searches outside your workspace are ignored.

200.description: The proposed spec and its eligibility preview.

totalLeads.description: Unique leads across the selected searches.

eligibleLeads.description: Leads reachable on the chosen platform — with an email for Smartlead, a LinkedIn URL for HeyReach.

issues.description: Blocking setup problems, in plain language. Empty means the campaign is publishable.

post.description:
Step two of two. Persists the reviewed spec and runs it against the provider: creates the list, pushes leads, builds the sequence, and sets the schedule.

Publishing stages everything but stops short of sending. The campaign lands in `awaiting_launch`, and a human has to call the launch endpoint to go live.

201.description: The campaign was created and is publishing.

get.description: The 50 most recent campaigns in the workspace, newest first.
The full campaign record, including the spec it was published from, the per-step execution plan with each step's status, and the launch audit stamp.

post.description:
The explicit go-live step. Starts the staged campaign at the provider and flips it to `live`.

The call is the approval: who launched it and when are stamped on the campaign row for the audit trail. Only campaigns sitting in `awaiting_launch` can be launched — anything else is a `409`. On provider failure the campaign moves to `failed` with the provider's message attached.
Creates a HeyReach list and pushes every lead with a LinkedIn URL into it — no sequence, no copy, no model involved. Use it when the sequence will be built in HeyReach's own builder.

scanIds.description: The searches to draw leads from. The list is named after the first one.

bearerAuth.description: A Revcenter API key: `Authorization: Bearer rvc_live_...`. Keys are scoped, rate limited per key, and metered per workspace.

sessionCookie.name: session
sessionCookie.description: A signed-in workspace session, sent as a browser cookie. Requests must include credentials, and act on the session's active workspace.

IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Deduplicates the billing event when a request is retried. Safe to send on every call.

SearchSurface.description: Which search surface to query. `endpoint` and `surface` are interchangeable.

ScanMode.description: `candidate` searches for people against a role. `client` discovers target companies first, then their decision-makers.

ExtractModel.description: Which model extracts criteria. Anything outside this allowlist is rejected. Omit to use the workspace default.

FundingSource.description: `platform` means Revcenter's own provider keys paid for the call and it counts as billable acquisition. `workspace_byok` means your workspace's own provider key did — the activity is recorded, but the vendor spend is yours, not billable overage.

request_id.description: Echoes an inbound `X-Request-Id` when you send one, otherwise generated. Always returned in the `X-Request-Id` header too.

MeteredEnvelope.description: The standard success envelope for billed endpoints.

Error.description: The error shape used by every `/v1` endpoint.

AppError.description: The error shape used by every `/api` endpoint. Flatter than the `/v1` shape, and `code` appears only where the UI branches on it.

ProviderPagination.description: Provider paging cursor, passed through untouched.

PersonSearchResult.description: A person as returned by search — enough to decide whether to spend an enrichment on them.

PersonProfile.description: A full profile. Provider fields pass through, so expect more keys than are listed here.

CompanyProfile.description: A full company record. Provider fields pass through, so expect more keys than are listed here.

Criteria.description:
The structured brief a search runs on. Every field is optional, but a search with no signal finds nothing useful.

The distinction that matters: `exclude_*` fields are hard and disqualify, while `avoid_*` fields are soft and only rank down. A great person at a firm you'd rather avoid still shows up; a person at an excluded firm never does.

family.description: Role family from the taxonomy. Off-taxonomy roles are kept as a title variant instead.

title_variants.description: Acceptable job titles. A quoted `title: "X"` in the brief always survives extraction and leads this list.

geo_radius_mi.description: Commute radius. Dropped automatically on country-level searches, where it is meaningless.

exclude_companies.description: Hard exclusion. Evaluated against search text too, so excluded people never reach paid enrichment.

avoid_titles.description: Soft negative — ranks down, never rejects.

languages_required.description: Hard requirement, kept separate from skills: holding a job title implies its competencies, but never implies a language.

rubric_weights.description: Relative emphasis per scoring dimension, compiled from what this brief stresses and locked to the run. The scorer clamps and renormalizes.

pulled.description: How many results have been pulled so far.

ScanStatus.description: A run that produced results finishes `complete` even if a late stage errored — partial results are not thrown away.

qualified.description: How many results cleared the qualification bar.

Run.description: One stage of the pipeline. The sequence is the audit trail for how a search reached its results.

hydrated.description: Whether the full profile was fetched, or only search-level data is known.

PublicCandidate.description: The redacted candidate shape used in shared shortlists. `email` and `phone` are always null.

error.description: Set when some or all job descriptions failed, e.g. `2/10 JDs failed`.

CampaignSpec.description: The reviewable campaign plan. Produced by the plan endpoint, sent back verbatim to publish.

platform.description: `smartlead` sends email and needs leads with emails. `heyreach` sends LinkedIn and needs leads with profile URLs.

external_campaign_id.description: The campaign's ID at the provider.

CampaignStatus.description: Publishing stages everything and stops at `awaiting_launch`. Only an explicit launch call moves it to `live`.

steps.description: Execution plan with live per-step status.

Unauthorized.description: No key, or the key is invalid, expired, or revoked.

error.message: API key is invalid, expired, or revoked.

InsufficientScope.description: The key authenticated but lacks the scope this endpoint requires.

ProviderUnavailable.description: The workspace has no usable provider key for this capability — it is either unprovisioned or switched off.

error.message: Web search is unavailable for this workspace.

RateLimited.description: The key exceeded its per-minute limit. Check `X-RateLimit-Reset` for when the window rolls over.

ProviderError.description: The upstream data source failed. Nothing is billed.

AppUnauthorized.description: Not signed in, no active workspace, or the account lacks the role this action needs. A frozen account gets `403` with code `frozen`.

AppNotFound.description: The record does not exist, or belongs to another workspace. The two are deliberately indistinguishable.

AppConflict.description: The record is in a state that does not allow this action.

AppProviderUnavailable.description: A capability this action needs is not connected for the workspace. The `code` names which one.

value.error: Search is unavailable for this workspace.
AI scoring is unavailable for this workspace.
No HeyReach API key configured — add one in Credentials.

AppUpstreamError.description: A downstream service or the database failed.
